title: A PHP cart array is one type doing duty as both list and map — the migration must resolve List vs Map, and money must not be a float
sourceContent:
<?php
// cart.php - a cart is a PHP array doing double duty as list AND map
function cartTotal($cart) {
    // $cart is associative: sku => ['qty' => int, 'price' => float]
    $total = 0.0;
    foreach ($cart as $sku => $line) {
        $total += $line['qty'] * $line['price'];
    }
    return $total;
}
notes: $cart is an associative array keyed by sku, each value a record-shaped sub-array {qty, price}. The migration must decide LinkedHashMap/Dictionary (order-preserving) vs a CartLine record — a single PHP type is doing both jobs. Separately, $total starts as a float (0.0): money as float is a precision trap; the target must use BigDecimal/decimal.
